title: $2.2 Billion for the Next Autoimmune Blockbuster?
summary: argenx plans to pay $2.2 billion in cash for Forte and its early anti-CD122 antibody FB102. The real test is not one Phase 1b p-value, but whether VYVGART's product success reflects a development engine the company can repeat.
source_status: Complete professional English adaptation of the approved Drugnews Chinese longform; transaction terms, clinical denominators, mechanism boundaries, Taiwan implications, references and disclaimers retained
cover_image_alt: argenx weighs a 2.2 billion dollar acquisition of Forte and the early anti-CD122 antibody FB102
card_image_alt: FB102 tests whether argenx can repeat the development playbook behind VYVGART
homepage_cover_image_alt: argenx moves from VYVGART commercial scale to an early-stage FB102 platform test
core_judgments: argenx has proved that it can scale VYVGART globally; acquiring FB102 tests whether its mechanism selection, indication sequencing and commercialization playbook can be repeated.
FB102's celiac disease and vitiligo Phase 1b signals support further investment but do not establish a second pipeline-in-a-product.
The $2.2 billion price will be justified by Phase 2 replication, a durable CD122 safety window and disciplined indication sequencing—not by the completeness of the acquisition narrative.
